draft.change: Add the gentilic יְבוּסִי under its attested place-name base יבוס. Its further derivation from בוס is uncertain.
draft.definition: A member of the people of Jebus. The definite singular can designate the people collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:16 lists the Jebusites among Canaan’s descendants. Judges 19:10–11 links the gentilic directly to the place named Jebus.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 10:16 places הַיְבוּסִי alongside the similarly formed הָאֱמֹרִי and הַגִּרְגָּשִׁי in the list of Canaan’s descendants. Judges 19:10–11 calls the place יְבוּס and then calls it the city of הַיְבוּסִי, identifying the base of the gentilic.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic noun. The ending ־ִי marks affiliation with Jebus. The singular denotes the people collectively.
analysis.sense: Jebusite, a member of the people of Jebus

draft.change: Add a standalone noun article for the gentilic אֱמֹרִי. The existing אמר article explicitly reserves this people’s name for its own entry.
draft.definition: An Amorite, a member of the Amorite people. The singular can designate the people collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:16 lists the Amorites among Canaan’s descendants. Genesis 14:13 applies the same gentilic to an individual, Mamre.

analysis.evidence: The repeated וְאֶת places הָאֱמֹרִי alongside the Jebusite and the Girgashite in the list of Canaan’s descendants. Genesis 10:18 calls these groups the clans of the Canaanite.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes אֱמֹרִי, a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state. The singular names the people collectively.

draft.change: Add the gentilic as a noun entry under its own consonants. The list of peoples establishes the ethnic sense, and the spelling provides no basis for the supplied root גרב.
draft.definition: Girgashite, used collectively for the Girgashite people.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:16 lists the Girgashites alongside the Jebusites and Amorites. Deuteronomy 7:1 explicitly counts them among seven nations.

analysis.evidence: The verse repeats the direct-object marker אֵת before each of three definite gentilics. הַגִּרְגָּשִׁי follows הַיְבוּסִי and הָאֱמֹרִי as the third people named in this part of Canaan’s genealogy.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic noun. The singular refers collectively to the people.
analysis.sense: The Girgashite people, listed among Canaan’s descendants.
